 She Was a Victim of Jeffrey Epstein. She Also Helped Him Find Other Girls.
 During the four years that Marina Lacerda was abused by Epstein, she introduced him to many of her friends.
 Marina Lacerda Credit... Gillian Laub for The New York Times

 By Jen Percy 
 Nov. 15, 2026 Marina Lacerda knew the friend who brought her to Jeffrey Epstein from the neighborhood. It was 2001, Marina was 13, and the friend was a couple of years older. They both lived near Steinway Street in Astoria, Queens, where people got dressed up just to walk around, stopping at the tanning salon, the shish kebab place and the barbershop, waving at friends riding up and down in their cars, pumping music. Marina’s block was “super Italian,” she told me. “Real Italians with plastic over their couches who were cooking pasta.” Around the corner were Egyptian and Romanian families, lots of Brazilian families like Marina’s.
 Listen to this article, read by Kirsten Potter
 Some of the girls around the corner formed a Spice Girls group and made up dances. Marina wore bell bottom jeans, a T-shirt with flowers and white platform sneakers printed with the Union Jack. It’s what she thought Sporty Spice would wear. It was also one of the only outfits she really had. Her mom, who worked as a cleaning lady, would take her to a thrift store and Payless, and that was it.
 Marina told her older friend, who was also Brazilian, everything about her life, including how badly she needed money. The friend wanted to help. “I have this really rich and powerful guy,” she said. “He’s really cool.” Marina could make $300 giving him a massage. The friend had met Epstein the same way — another girl from the neighborhood introduced her. “The only thing is you have to take off your top,” she said. “It’s like being in a bikini.”
 Marina remembers taking a cab to Manhattan with her friend, because Epstein paid for it. She knew there were skyscrapers in the city, but she didn’t know there were mansions. She had never been in a rich person’s home before. She walked into the townhouse on East 71st Street wearing the same clothes she wore almost every day, looking like Sporty Spice.
 Marina and her friend took an elevator to the third floor and waited in the massage room, where the ceiling was painted to look like the sky. She loved the sky! It was her favorite thing. When she was a little girl, still living in Brazil, Marina would sometimes get carsick on drives with her grandparents, and they would tell her to lie down in the back seat and look up at the sky. It always made her feel better. Her mom had already left for America, but she felt safe looking up at the sky, thinking about how they were under the same roof of stars.
